THING.description: root: any node type is-a THING

METHOD.description: a named modeling approach/theory/law/model (e.g. μ(I) rheology, kinetic theory, NGF, DEM, RFT)

PARAMETER.description: a named physical quantity/constant/coefficient in equations (e.g. μ, I, d, P, τ, g, ρ_s, T, A, ξ, μ_s, b)

PHENOMENON.description: a physical effect/behavior methods capture (e.g. nonlocal creep, thin-body strengthening, secondary rheology, segregation, clogging)

PROPERTY.description: a generic physical property/quantity not fitting the above (kept for residual cases)

constitutive_law.description: a constitutive law relating output quantity/quantities to >=1 input quantity (n-ary)
constitutive_law.semantic_boundary: a FORMAL/QUANTITATIVE law output=f(inputs+params), stated as a formula or explicit functional relation. NOT a prose 'X depends on Y' (that is influences), NOT a definition (defines), NOT a measurement setup (measures).

influences.description: one quantity influences / depends on >=1 target quantity (n-ary, general dependence)
influences.semantic_boundary: X functionally depends on / varies with Y (a genuine causal or scaling dependence). NOT a co-listing of parallel items (composed_of), NOT a classification (defines), NOT 'we tested X' (measures), NOT 'X is part of Y' (composed_of).

defines.description: one entity is defined-as / identified-with / named-by another (definitional identity, n-ary)
defines.semantic_boundary: a DEFINITIONAL identity: X is defined as / is / denotes / is named / is classified into Y. NOT a structural part-of (composed_of), NOT a functional dependence (influences). 'X is analogous to Y' is a CLAIM not a definition.

composed_of.description: one whole is composed-of / part-of >=1 component (n-ary composition)
composed_of.semantic_boundary: STRUCTURAL composition: parts that make up a whole (model A = B + C). NOT classification (defines), NOT 'X has control params' (influences), NOT experimental setup description, NOT 'we tested X by doing Y'.

measures.description: a quantity is measured by / characterizes >=1 measure
measures.semantic_boundary: a measurement/evaluation relation: X is measured/evaluated by instrument/method Y. NOT a functional law (constitutive_law), NOT a dependence (influences).

claim_relation.semantic_boundary: a DISCOURSE relation between claims/findings (supports/contrasts/outperforms). NOT a method-to-method development (extends/improves/compares — those are evolution), NOT a measurement (measures).

extends.semantic_boundary: X GENERALIZES Y (X extends Y's scope/regime/params; X is a direct technical extension of Y). NOT improves (X need not be more accurate, just broader), NOT background (X is a direct technical inheritance, not a motivation citation), NOT claim_relation (this is method-to-method).

improves.description: X improves Y's accuracy/applicability, resolving Y's limitation
improves.semantic_boundary: X RESOLVES a limitation of Y (X is more accurate/applicable BECAUSE it fixes something Y fails at; first-principles vs phenomenological = improves). NOT compares (X is NOT a parallel different-mechanism alternative; X builds on Y and is better), NOT extends (X is better not just broader).

compares.semantic_boundary: A and B are put side by side: either (i) PARALLEL different-mechanism alternatives with overlapping scope (both model the same phenomenon, different assumptions), or (ii) THEORY-vs-EXPERIMENT / prediction-vs-observation validation ('data compared with predictions', 'simulations agree with experiments', 'in contrast with'), or (iii) equivalence/contrast of formulations ('equivalent', 'the same as', 'rather than'). NOT improves (neither fixes the other's limitation), NOT extends (neither generalizes the other).

replaces.semantic_boundary: X SUBSTITUTES Y outright (X is used INSTEAD of Y; Y is retired). NOT improves (replaces = Y is gone, improves = Y still used + X better).

adapts.description: X adapts Y to a new scenario
adapts.semantic_boundary: X PORTS Y to a NEW scenario/regime/domain Y wasn't designed for (adaptation of Y's mechanism). NOT extends (adapts = new scenario, extends = broader scope within same setting).

background.semantic_boundary: X cites Y as MOTIVATION/prior context only (Y inspired X but X is NOT a direct technical extension/inheritance of Y). NOT extends (no direct technical lineage), NOT improves (no limitation fix).

contrasts_with.description: A discourse relation where one theory/approach is explicitly contrasted with another, often to highlight differences in assumptions, scope, or predictions. This is distinct from compares (which is about side-by-side evaluation) and claim_relation (which is about support/opposition between claims).
contrasts_with.semantic_boundary: contrasts_with = explicit opposition between two theories/approaches, NOT side-by-side evaluation (compares) and NOT support/opposition between claims (claim_relation).

validates_against.description: A relation where a theory/model's predictions are validated or checked against experimental or observational data. This is distinct from 'compares' (which includes theory-vs-experiment as one subtype) because it specifically emphasizes the validation/evaluation aspect, not just side-by-side comparison.
validates_against.semantic_boundary: Use only when the core action is testing/evaluating a model or theory against data; not for mere side-by-side comparison or general agreement.

assesses_accuracy_of.description: X provides means to assess/evaluate the accuracy of Y (a methodological relation where one approach serves as a benchmark or reference to evaluate another's accuracy). This is distinct from compares (which is side-by-side) and improves (which implies fixing limitations).
assesses_accuracy_of.semantic_boundary: Use when one method is explicitly used as a benchmark/reference to test another’s accuracy; not for side-by-side comparison (compares) or fixing flaws (improves).

substitutes_in.description: A mathematical/formal relation where one operator, expression, or quantity can be substituted for another in a specific context without changing the result. This is distinct from replaces (which implies outright retirement of the old entity) and defines (which implies definitional identity).
substitutes_in.semantic_boundary: Use substitutes_in only when one thing can be swapped for another in a specific operation or proof; not for replacing/retiring (replaces) or defining equivalence (defines).

analogous_to.description: A relation where one mathematical expression, integral, or quantity is given in a similar way to another, indicating structural or methodological analogy without implying derivation or definitional identity.
analogous_to.semantic_boundary: Use for explicit “analogous to” or “similar in form/method” comparisons; NOT for derivation, definition, or mere co-occurrence.

lacks_comparison.description: X lacks comparison with Y, indicating that no prior work exists for comparison, highlighting novelty or absence of benchmark.
lacks_comparison.semantic_boundary: Use when explicitly stating no comparison or benchmark exists for X, not when comparing X to Y or noting a lack of evidence.

describes.description: A relation where one entity (typically a model or theory) describes or accounts for a phenomenon or system. This is distinct from 'influences' (which implies causal dependence) and 'constitutive_law' (which requires formal quantitative relations).
describes.semantic_boundary: Applies when a model/theory explains or accounts for a phenomenon, not when it merely influences it or states a quantitative law.

sets_parameter_value.description: A relation where a parameter or variable is assigned a specific numerical value or set to a particular condition in an experimental or simulation setup. This is distinct from 'defines' (which implies definitional identity) and 'measures' (which implies measurement/evaluation).
sets_parameter_value.semantic_boundary: Use when a parameter is explicitly assigned a number or condition in setup; NOT for defining its meaning or reporting a measured outcome.
